title: Risotto con Funghi Porcini
subtitle: Dried porcini risotto with fresh mushrooms and Parmesan
excerpt: Risotto con funghi porcini uses dried porcini mushrooms for concentrated flavour and fresh chestnut mushrooms for texture. The porcini soaking liquid goes into the risotto as part of the stock. The result is deeply savoury, earthy, and rich.
sourceNotes: Porcini mushroom risotto is one of the most classic Italian risotti, made across the north from Piedmont to Veneto in autumn when fresh porcini are in season. The technique of using dried porcini to boost flavour when fresh are unavailable is standard.

content.text: The dried porcini are the key ingredient here: they provide a concentrated, almost meaty depth that fresh mushrooms alone cannot match. Soak them in just-boiled water for 20 minutes, then strain the soaking liquid carefully through a fine sieve -- it contains fine grit that must be removed before it goes into the risotto.

items.prepNote: soaked in 300ml just-boiled water for 20 minutes, then strained (soaking liquid reserved)

content.text: Soak {{mushrooms-porcini-dried}} porcini in 300ml of just-boiled water for 20 minutes. Strain through a fine sieve, squeezing the mushrooms. Chop the soaked porcini roughly. Combine the strained soaking liquid with the {{vegetable-stock}} stock and keep hot.

Heat 2 tbsp of the {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a frying pan over high heat. Fry {{mushrooms-chestnut}} chestnut mushrooms in two batches until golden brown. Season with {{salt-table}} salt. Set aside.

Heat the remaining oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and the chopped porcini and cook for 2 minutes. Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes.

Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed. Add the hot mushroom-stock mixture a ladleful at a time, stirring for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente. Stir in the fried chestnut mushrooms.
Remove from the heat. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter and {{parmesan}} Parmesan. Season with {{black-pepper}} pepper and remaining {{salt-table}} salt. Serve at once.

items.cause: The porcini soaking liquid was not strained finely enough.
items.fix: Strain the porcini liquid through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a piece of damp kitchen paper or muslin. Dried porcini always contain fine sand. Stop before the last tablespoon of liquid at the bottom of the soaking bowl.

content.text: Porcini mushroom risotto is made across northern Italy in September and October when fresh porcini come into season. The dried version extends the season year-round. It is one of the most popular risotti outside Italy as well as within it, partly because the ingredients are straightforward and the flavour is exceptional. In Piedmont it is sometimes made with a knob of butter and a grating of white truffle at the finish, which is the finest version.
